question.problem:
Consider the equation $2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-{4}^{∘})-1=0$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ are written in **ascending order**, what are their values?

${x}_{1}=${{field-1}}${}^{∘},\,$
${x}_{2}=${{field-2}}${}^{∘},\,$
${x}_{3}=${{field-3}}${}^{∘},\,$
${x}_{4}=${{field-4}}${}^{∘}$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-{4}^{∘})-1 & =0 \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-{4}^{∘}) & =1 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-{4}^{∘}) & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-{4}^{∘} & ={30}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & 2x-{4}^{∘} & ={150}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ={34}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} & \, & \, & 2x & ={154}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} \\ x & ={17}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={77}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={17}^{∘}$ and $x={77}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x={197}^{∘}$ and $x={257}^{∘}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x={17}^{∘},{77}^{∘},{197}^{∘},{257}^{∘}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
{x}_{1}={17}^{∘},\,{x}_{2}={77}^{∘},\,{x}_{3}={197}^{∘},\,{x}_{4}={257}^{∘}
$$
